question: How do SWE-2 Medium and Max compare when newly constructed, withheld software-repair tasks are intentionally pushed beyond the difficulty of the earlier benchmark cases?
secondary_questions: Does additional reasoning effort improve complete behavioral repair on the stress-test cases?
Do visible-test success and held-out behavioral success disagree more often when the cases require cross-module reasoning?
How do Medium and Max compare on wall time, observable steps, tool calls, tokens, patch breadth, and workspace churn?

cases.category: dependency graph and transitive cache invalidation
asynchronous cancellation and worker lifecycle consistency
incremental framed-protocol parsing and recovery state machine
transactional multi-stage operation and compensation ordering
event subscription lifecycle and reentrant dispatch

intervention_policy: zero substantive human or Codex assistance; no retries for ordinary agent failures
success_rule: TASK_SUCCESS is 1 only when public, held-out behavioral, and regression suites all pass; evaluator infrastructure errors are recorded separately as EVALUATION_ERROR.

limits.session_termination: terminate at 5400 seconds or when Devin exits; close the session before evaluator access
limits.infrastructure_timeout_behavior: classify a watchdog or service timeout as infrastructure only when the harness or service is at fault; an agent that reaches the limit is an agent outcome

capture: model, reasoning effort, configuration, and byte-identical task prompt hash
UTC start/end, elapsed wall time, observable steps, tool calls, prompt/completion tokens, usage, cost, and ACUs when available
stdout, stderr, session export, termination reason, final filesystem patch, and source/generated workspace churn
public, held-out, and regression evaluator results, intervention count, and evaluator notes

isolation.execution: same frozen isolated Devin architecture used for E002/E003; no shared infrastructure changes
isolation.workspace: one fresh sanitized buggy workspace, read-write
isolation.credentials: minimum Devin credential file only, read-only
isolation.network: existing E002 internal network and restricted Devin-service proxy; no dependency installation during agent session
isolation.evaluator: outside the container and unavailable until the session is closed

novelty_boundary: The five E005 benchmark instances, defect implementations, prompts, reference fixes, and held-out evaluations were newly constructed for this experiment and withheld from Devin until execution. Training-data absence is not claimed.
embargo: Private buggy/fixed trees, reference patches, held-out tests, evaluator metadata, construction notes, and solution-bearing validation remain local until all ten E005 runs close.
